rows.name: Reset - power-on / RESET entry (boot, init, then idle loop)
rows.notes: Where the CPU starts at power-on. Found by read_memory of the 6502 RESET vector: $FFFC/$FFFD = $00 $80 -> $8000. Disassembly of $8000 shows the canonical boot sequence: $8000 SEI / $8001 CLD (mask IRQs, clear decimal); $8002 LDA #$10 / $8004 STA $2000 (PPUCTRL, NMI off while initializing); $8007 LDX #$FF / $8009 TXS (stack to $01FF); $800A-$8013 LDA $2002 / BPL twice (poll PPUSTATUS to wait two vblanks for PPU warm-up); $8014-$8029 checks the continue marker $07FF == $A5 and picks the boot state via $90CC; $802E STA $4011 (APU DMC); $8031 STA $0770; $8036 STA $07FF=$A5 and $8039 $07A7=$A5 (write the resume markers); $803E LDA #$0F / STA $4015 (APU enable); $8043 LDA #$06 / STA $2001 (PPUMASK, both layers on); $8046 JSR $8220 / $8049 JSR $8E19 (init); $804C INC $0774 (frame counter); $804F-$8054 LDA $0778 / ORA #$80 / JSR $8EED (enable NMI); $8057 JMP $8057 - the routine hands control to an infinite wait loop where the CPU idles and all per-frame work happens in the NMI (the game is NMI-driven; the main thread never leaves $8057). The instruction that ends the boot job is the transfer to the idle loop at $8057. Emulator proof: reset_emulator, then get_cpu_state returned PC $8057 (with a fresh cycle counter and the title screen restored) - i.e. the CPU had run the code at $8000 and settled exactly on the JMP $8057 target. Before the reset the emulator was also sitting at $8057/$8058 during normal play, confirming the main thread stays in this loop. No direct JSR/JMP to $8000 exists; the RESET vector is the only entry, as expected.

rows.name: NMI - per-frame interrupt handler (PPU setup, OAM DMA, game logic)
rows.notes: The vblank/NMI handler, i.e. the whole per-frame engine. Found by read_memory of the 6502 NMI vector: $FFFA/$FFFB = $82 $80 -> $8082. Disassembly $8082-$8181 (ends RTI at $8181, 0x100 bytes) shows what it does each frame: $8082 reads $0778, AND #$7F, stores, AND #$7E / $808C STA $2000 (PPUCTRL: nametable select + sprite size, NMI bit cleared during setup); $80A3 STA $2001 (PPUMASK from $0779); $80A6 LDA $2002 (read PPUSTATUS, reset the vblank/sprite-0 latch); $80B3 LDA #$02 / STA $4014 (OAM DMA page 2 -> hardware sprites); $80B6-$80C3 indexes tables $805A/$806D by VRAM-queue state $0773 and JSR $8EDD (the VRAM update/queue transfer); $80E4 JSR $F2D0, $80E7 JSR $8E5C, $80EA JSR $8182, $80ED JSR $8F97 (per-frame game logic: input/player/objects/sound); $80F0-$8138 the frame timers (decrements $0747, $077F, the $0780,X array) and the controller-shift logic; $815C/$8165 write the scroll to $2005 (PPUSCROLL x then y from $073F/$0740); $8168-$817E push $0778, STA $2000, and finally ORA #$80 / STA $2000 to re-enable NMI, then $8181 RTI. What does the job of a NMI: the OAM DMA write to $4014 at $80B3 plus the PPUCTRL/PPUMASK/PPUSCROLL writes, all done once per frame. Emulator proof: trace_writes on CPU $2000 for 60 frames returned 60 writes from PC $808F, 60 from $816F and 60 from $8181 - a full set of PPUCTRL writes every frame - and all three PCs lie inside $8082-$8181. Since the main thread idles at $8057, every frame's hardware/vblank work is this handler.

rows.name: GameEngine - per-frame dispatch on GameMode ($0770)
rows.notes: The game-mode dispatch. Runs once per frame from the NMI: at CPU $8175 the NMI does JSR $8212, guarded by LDA $0776 / LSR A / BCS (skip) at $816F-$8173, so it only runs when OperMode bit 0 is clear. Entry $8212: LDA $0770 (GameMode) ; JSR $8E04 (jump engine), and the 4-entry target table follows at $8218: $8231 (mode 0 = title screen / attract demo), $AEDC (mode 1 = game / in a level), $838B (mode 2 = victory), $9218 (mode 3 = game over). $8E04 is the jump engine: ASL A / TAY / PLA / STA $04 / PLA / STA $05 / INY / LDA ($04),Y / STA $06 / INY / LDA ($04),Y / STA $07 / JMP ($0006) - it pops the return address (the table at $8218) and uses A as a byte index to fetch the target and JMP indirectly. Both $8231 and $AEDC are themselves secondary dispatchers (each starts LDA $0772 / JSR $8E04). Found with no reference by searching PRG for LDA $0770: the only match in the per-frame path is $8212, which the NMI calls. Emulator proof: play_input/watch on $0770 read 0 on the title/attract screen and flipped to 1 exactly when the second Start began World 1-1; the mapping's LoseLife sets $0770=3 at game over, which is mode 3 -> $9218. Table bytes at $8218: $8231,$AEDC,$838B,$9218.

rows.name: LoadAreaPalette - pick the area's background+sprite palette when a level starts
rows.notes: The routine that loads an area's background and sprite colours at level start. It is step 9 of the level-initialization state machine at $8567 (LDA $073C / JSR $8E04 with the address table at $856D; one of its targets is $85BF). Entry $85BF: LDY $074E (area palette index) ; LDX $85BB,Y (selector table at $85BB = $01,$02,$03,$04) ; STX $0773 (VRAM-buffer selector) ; JMP $8745. The NMI then does at $80B6-$80C3: LDX $0773 / LDA $805A,X / STA $00 / LDA $806D,X / STA $01 / JSR $8EDD, and that writes the selected PRG buffer to the PPU through $2006/$2007. The four selectable buffers are complete [3F 00 20 <32 palette bytes> 00] records in PRG: $8CA4 (selector 1, dark/underground-like), $8CC8 (selector 2, the normal overworld palette used by World 1-1), $8CEC (selector 3), $8D10 (selector 4). Found with no reference: a trace_writes read on the selector table $85BB during a forced World 1-1 reload (time-up death) returned exactly one access - PC $85C5, right after LDX $85BB,Y at $85C2, reading address $85BC (=$85BB+$074E with $074E=1), value 2 - i.e. this routine chose the overworld block for 1-1. Corroboration: a trace_writes read over $8CA0-$8D27 during another reload caught the NMI writer reading $8CC8-$8CEB (PCs $8E96/$8E9C/$8EBB/$8EE2) and copying it to $2007; writing $0773=1 by hand while paused then step_frame 1 swapped the entire level to the $8CA4 palette (pipes blue/pink, ground green - screenshot) and $0773=2 restored the normal overworld colours. $074E read 1 during World 1-1 play.

rows.name: WriteVRAMBuffer - NMI routine that writes palette/VRAM via $2006/$2007
rows.notes: The code that actually puts the area palette on the hardware, i.e. the $2006/$2007 writer the task suspected ("possibly from a RAM buffer that the frame interrupt copies"). The NMI calls it at $80C3 with $00/$01 already pointing at the buffer chosen from tables $805A/$806D by the selector $0773. Entry $8EDD: LDX $2002 ; LDY #$00 ; LDA ($00),Y ; BNE $8E92 - a zero first byte ends the transfer with two STA $2005 and RTS. The non-empty path at $8E92: STA $2006 (address high) ; INY ; LDA ($00),Y ; STA $2006 (address low) ; INY ; LDA ($00),Y (control/length) ; ASL A ; PHA ; (bit 7 of the control byte toggles a PPUCTRL bit via $8EA9 JSR $8EED, which stores $0778/$2000) ; ASL A / LSR A / LSR A / TAX (length) ; loop at $8EB6-$8EBF: LDA ($00),Y / STA $2007 / DEX / BNE ; then $8EC1-$8ECB advances the pointer by Y and the next record is processed. For a palette record [3F 00 20 ...] this sets PPUADDR to $3F00 and writes the following 32 bytes to $2007, loading all 8 hardware palettes (4 BG + 4 sprite) in one go. Found with no reference from the trace of the palette data (read PCs $8E96/$8E9C/$8EBB/$8EE2) and from a search for LDA #$3F / STA $2006, which occurs only at $8ECD in this routine. Proven: forcing $0773=1,2 by hand and stepping one frame changed the rendered palette accordingly.

rows.name: area_palette_index
rows.notes: Index into the area-palette selector table $85BB (=$01,$02,$03,$04), read by LoadAreaPalette at $85BF. World 1-1 holds 1 -> selector 2 -> the overworld palette block at $8CC8. Found with no reference: read 1 throughout World 1-1 play (play_input watch) and the value read from the table during the 1-1 reload was $85BC (=$85BB+1) = 2.

rows.name: vram_buffer_selector
rows.notes: Selects which buffer the NMI's VRAM transfer ($8EDD) copies. The NMI reads $805A,X and $806D,X with X=$0773 and drops the result into $00/$01. Entries: 0 -> $0301, 1 -> $8CA4, 2 -> $8CC8, 3 -> $8CEC, 4 -> $8D10 (four [3F 00 20 <32 palette bytes> 00] palette blocks), 5 -> $0300, 6 -> $0341 (RAM buffers). The NMI clears it to 0 every frame at $80DB, so it is a one-frame request. Found with no reference: trace_writes on $0773 for 600 frames showed 598 writes of 0 from PC $80DE (the NMI clear) plus a single nonzero write from the level-init palette step; the pointer tables were read from PRG at $805A/$806D.

rows.name: How a level's colours reach the PPU (World 1-1 example)
rows.notes: Chain proven with no reference. Level-init state machine $8567 (LDA $073C / JSR $8E04, table $856D) step 9 -> $85BF (LoadAreaPalette): LDY $074E / LDX $85BB,Y / STX $0773. Table $85BB = $01,$02,$03,$04; 1-1 has $074E=1 so $0773=2. Next NMI ($80B6-$80C3): LDX $0773 / LDA $805A,X / STA $00 / LDA $806D,X / STA $01 / JSR $8EDD. The pointer tables $805A/$806D map selector 1..4 to the four PRG palette records $8CA4,$8CC8,$8CEC,$8D10, each [3F 00 20 <32 palette bytes> 00]. $8EDD/$8E92 writes the record: STA $2006 (=$3F) / STA $2006 (=$00) then loops LDA ($00),Y / STA $2007 for the 32 bytes, setting all 4 BG + 4 sprite hardware palettes. Evidence: trace read on $85BB during a 1-1 reload = PC $85C5 reading $85BC value 2; trace read over $8CA0-$8D27 during a reload = PC $8E96/$8E9C/$8EBB/$8EE2 reading $8CC8-$8CEB; manual write $0773=1 then step_frame changed the whole palette to $8CA4 (screenshot), $0773=2 restored it. The live PPU palette for 1-1 equals the $8CC8 block (with $3F00 backdrop $22 written by the record's first byte being $0F and the engine's own backdrop write).
